profile.name: Mateusz Ciszek
profile.bio: I build games and the systems behind them. My work spans 2D and 3D gameplay, reusable Unity tools, and Android applications. I care about responsive interactions, maintainable code, and giving a good idea room to grow.

projects.title: Bonnie's Farmville
projects.summary: A Unity farming-economy minigame for the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2 title 40in1 GameCollection Vol3, featuring a data-driven farming grid and autonomous companion AI.
projects.imageAlt: Bonnie's Farmville title artwork featuring a rabbit with a watering can, vegetable plots, and farm animals
overview: Bonnie's Farmville connects a data-driven world grid with autonomous companion AI. Gameplay configuration is separated from runtime logic, so new farm layouts, crops, items, prices, and upgrades can be authored without rewriting the underlying systems.

sections.title: Data-driven farming grid
sections.summary: A reusable authoring pipeline that turns visual tile painting into structured runtime data for farming interactions and navigation.
paragraphs: I created a tile-based data layer that converts painted Unity Tilemaps into reusable gameplay properties for individual grid cells. Designers can mark diggable areas, walkable paths, water sources, placement zones, and NPC obstacles directly in the Scene view. An editor component collects these layers into a serialized ScriptableObject containing the coordinates and property values used at runtime.

The runtime grid manager translates between world and cell coordinates, combines multiple properties for each cell, validates player actions, and stores temporary state such as dug soil, watering, planted seeds, and crop growth. The same data source is shared with other systems.

image.alt: Unity Scene views showing painted Diggable and Path tilemap layers beside a serialized grid-property list in the Inspector

sections.caption: Painted Diggable and Path layers are converted into a serialized per-cell property list used by gameplay systems at runtime.

sections.title: Companion AI and pathfinding
sections.summary: Lightweight companion behaviour combining authored navigation data, A* routing, movement states, avoidance, and recovery logic.
paragraphs: I developed an unlockable companion system with grid-aware A* pathfinding. Pets roam near the player, begin following when the distance becomes too large, and stop at a comfortable range instead of overlapping the character. Their movement queries the same walkability and obstacle data used by the farming grid.

The behaviour includes safe spawn selection, player avoidance, directional animation, idle timing, failed-path handling, and teleport recovery when the companion is separated by an extreme distance. Paths are calculated only when a new destination is selected, avoiding unnecessary searches every frame while still responding to player movement.

image.alt: In-game companion beside the player, paired with the authored navigation tilemap and serialized grid data in Unity

sections.caption: The companion uses the authored Path and obstacle layers for A* navigation while roaming near and following the player.

sections.title: Item and crop definitions
sections.summary: Shared ScriptableObject definitions connect inventory, shops, crops, and progression.
paragraphs: I built a shared item-data pipeline that drives inventory limits, seed prices, crop rewards, tool tiers, and shop presentation. Item and crop definitions are stored in ScriptableObjects, making it straightforward to add new items without changing the underlying gameplay systems.

image.alt: Runtime crop shop beside Unity Inspector panels for Item and Crop ScriptableObject configuration

sections.caption: The runtime shop uses shared Item and Crop ScriptableObject definitions for prices, inventory limits, crop rewards, and upgrades.

projects.title: Power Washer Hero
projects.summary: A reusable Unity cleaning pipeline with GPU-painted dirt masks, compute-shader coverage tracking, and editor tools for configuring multi-part cleaning targets.
projects.imageAlt: Power Washer Hero title artwork showing a car being pressure-washed in a garage
overview: I built a reusable Unity cleaning pipeline with GPU-painted dirt masks, compute-shader coverage tracking, per-part and overall progression, animated UI feedback, and configurable procedural dirt materials. Editor tools rapidly convert multi-part models into calibrated cleaning targets.

sections.title: GPU-driven washable surfaces
paragraphs: Each washable mesh owns a runtime dirt mask stored in a RenderTexture. The pressure washer projects a world-space brush onto the target, while a custom shader uses surface normals to reject backfaces and prevent the spray from cleaning through corners. Dirt is removed cumulatively, producing persistent, localized cleaning across complex shapes.

image.alt: Power Washer cleaning pipeline showcase with gameplay, Unity material setup, and per-part calibration data

sections.caption: GPU-driven cleaning connects persistent dirt masks, per-part progress, and reusable authoring tools.

sections.title: Real-time coverage measurement
paragraphs: A compute shader reduces the dirt-mask pixels into coverage data. The result is converted into a normalized completion percentage for every individual car part, giving the game accurate progress values without relying on trigger counts or hand-authored checkpoints.

sections.title: Configurable dirt materials
paragraphs: The washable surface shader blends clean albedo with procedural dirt using tunable noise, tint, scale, opacity, smoothness, and metallic controls. This lets one cleaning system support varied materials and grime patterns while preserving the original look of each model.

image.alt: Procedural dirt shader breakdown showing Unity material settings, clean albedo, dirt noise, a runtime paint mask, and the layered result

sections.caption: Clean albedo and procedural dirt are blended through a runtime paint mask, with configurable noise and surface properties.

sections.title: Reachability calibration tool
paragraphs: A generated ScriptableObject stores the maximum realistically cleanable percentage for every mesh part and records the last percentage reached during testing. Designers can compensate for UV seams, hidden geometry, or inaccessible pixels, so a visually clean part can still reach 100% in gameplay.

screenshots.alt: Partially cleaned car with individual part percentages and overall cleaning progress.
A multi-part cleaning target with localized dirt removal and overall progress feedback.
Front view of a car with cleaned patches revealing its paint and windshield beneath the dirt.

projects.title: 100 in 1 Game Collection
projects.summary: A selection of mini-games I designed and programmed in Unity and C# for 100 in 1 Game Collection on Nintendo Switch and Steam.
projects.imageAlt: 100 in 1 Game Collection cover featuring a collage of its arcade mini-games
overview: These are the mini-games I designed and programmed for the collection, along with selected mechanics and technical contributions.

miniGames.title: Rabbit Hopper
miniGames.description: A Frogger-inspired crossing game with traffic that reacts to the player: school buses slow down nearby, while sports cars accelerate. Fire hydrants launch the player forward, creating shortcuts through the level.

miniGames.title: Space Doggo
miniGames.description: A Pang-inspired arcade game in which a space-faring dog battles waves of bouncing aliens. Blaster upgrades and power-ups help the player clear each level.

miniGames.title: Sweets Crusher
miniGames.description: Control food claws along the X-axis to grab descending sweets and reposition them into vertical match-three combinations. Clear the board and use power-ups to prevent it from overflowing.

miniGames.title: Reversi
miniGames.description: Classic Reversi with an AI opponent designed to offer a competitive but approachable challenge.
technicalNotes: AI balancing: the main challenge was making the opponent strategically capable without making it frustratingly difficult to beat.

miniGames.title: Cosmic Painter
miniGames.description: A Qix-inspired game where a painter claims sections of a canvas with a magical brush. Roaming ink containers undo progress, while power-ups provide temporary boosts and protection.

miniGames.title: Dinosaurs Mania
miniGames.description: An Elasto Mania-inspired motorcycle game set in a prehistoric world. Precise bike control and physics-based movement let players climb, flip, and ride across challenging terrain.

miniGames.title: CatPotionCraft
miniGames.description: A potion-themed puzzle game starring a magical cat. Aim potions and match colorful ingredients to clear the board while balancing quick reactions with careful planning.

miniGames.title: Bombastic Witch
miniGames.description: A Bomberman-inspired game where a witch uses explosive spells to fight enchanted crows. Navigate grid-based arenas, destroy obstacles, and set traps.
technicalNotes: Analog-stick grid movement: interpolated movement and trajectory adjustments near obstacles guide the player around corners and reduce abrupt stops.
Versus-mode features: Ring of Fire and teleport mechanics.

miniGames.title: Dungeon Dragons
miniGames.description: A Battle City-inspired game where a dragon defends its land against invading Vikings. Breathe fire, destroy obstacles, and outmaneuver enemies in maze-like arenas.

projects.title: A Game About Clicking A Rock
projects.summary: One rock. A growing mining operation. A 3D incremental game about turning a simple click into an automated empire.
projects.imageAlt: A Game About Clicking A Rock title artwork with colorful desert cliffs, ore rocks, and mine tracks

videos.title: A Game About Clicking A Rock · Trailer

overview: A personal Unity project built around mining, upgrades, and automated workers. Available to explore on itch.io, with a Steam store page for the upcoming PC release.
Built data-driven ore balancing and progression using ScriptableObjects, event-driven resource updates, English/Polish localization, and a guided first-run tutorial.
Implemented autosave, JSON save/load, exportable encoded save codes, and finite-state-machine worker AI with node-based movement.

screenshots.alt: Workers mining colorful ore around the mine entrance, with hit effects and resource counters.

Magical Gemstone Shop offering extraction, pickaxe, and ore upgrades.
Character customization with a 3D preview and hat, skin, pants, and shoes options.
Workers gathering ore around a mine entrance in a snowy landscape.
Ore selling shop with quantity sliders, sale values, and a cat shopkeeper.

projects.title: MaCster Unity Framework
projects.summary: A modular foundation for gameplay, from inventories and interactions to node-based dialogue tools.
overview: A private C#/Unity library of reusable gameplay systems and editor tools.
Includes saving, object pooling, inventory management, shop/cart logic, 3D interaction, player movement, and dialogue graphs.
Uses ScriptableObject data, interface-based contracts, and event-driven UI flows. The xNode dialogue tooling supports conditional branches, player responses, action nodes, and runtime playback.

projects.title: Mobile E-Commerce App
projects.summary: An Android shopping application covering products, purchases, and order tracking.
overview: Built a mobile e-commerce application in Kotlin with Android Studio and Google Firebase.
Implemented product and order management, user registration, purchasing, and order tracking/history. Designed and implemented the Firebase database.

projects.title: Mobile Game · Engineering Thesis
projects.summary: A working Android game prototype exploring engagement and player retention through academic research.
overview: Bachelor’s thesis: Using Social Engineering Methods in a Mobile Game.
Developed the game concept, MVP design, and a working Android prototype with a responsive UI that adapts to different screen resolutions.
Researched scientific literature and mobile games to analyze engagement, retention, and monetization techniques.

projects.title: Learning to Find a Path
projects.summary: A reinforcement learning experiment that trains an agent to navigate toward a moving target.
overview: A Unity/C# proof of concept using reinforcement learning to train an AI agent to navigate toward a dynamically changing target.
